task: Independently assess quantitative transport mechanisms for concrete probability/statistical-physics systems.
overall_status: known mechanism reconstructed; no novelty claim

claims.claim: For a finite full-support product law with single-site heat-bath updates at rate one, if positive weights satisfy sum_i w_i c_ij <= (1-kappa) w_j for every changed coordinate j, then the continuous-time semigroup contracts W1 in weighted Hamming cost by exp(-kappa t).
claims.scope: Exact one-site conditionals; finite product state space; arbitrary initial probability laws.
claims.evidence: Maximal same-site coupling, coordinatewise influence telescoping, generator drift, and Gronwall inequality.

claims.claim: For symmetric pairwise Ising interactions, c_ij <= tanh(beta*abs(J_ij)); hence max_j sum_i tanh(beta*abs(J_ij)) <= 1-kappa yields Hamming W1 contraction exp(-kappa t) and TV mixing time at most kappa^{-1} log(n/epsilon) at rate one per site.
claims.scope: Finite undirected Ising graphs, arbitrary finite external fields, beta >= 0.
claims.evidence: Exact conditional-logit formula and maximization of the Bernoulli TV difference; diameter-to-TV conversion.

claims.claim: A row-sum influence bound in the output-site-by-changed-site convention does not certify contraction of the standard common-site maximal coupling in unweighted Hamming distance.
claims.status: finite counterexample verified; limited to this coupling claim
claims.scope: Four-spin Ising star with b=atanh(1/2), center field 6, and zero leaf fields.
claims.evidence: The maximum row sum is 1/2 while a center-only disagreement has coupled Hamming drift +1/2; see star_check.py. Alternative couplings are not ruled out.

claims.claim: The contraction and rapid-mixing mechanism is established prior art, so this work is not presented as novel.
claims.scope: Path coupling and dependency-matrix criteria for Glauber dynamics.

charged_costs: General worst-case single-site influences may require exponential boundary enumeration unless a symbolic upper bound is available.
Rate-one-per-site continuous time has total event rate n; certified simulation requires expected O((n/kappa)*log(D_w/(w_min*epsilon))) single-site events.
Per-update conditional-sampling cost is model-dependent and not hidden by the contraction theorem.
limitations: The influence condition is sufficient, not necessary.
Failure of the weighted column condition does not establish slow mixing.
The finite star refutes an inference for the usual common-site coupling, not every coupling or Hamming-Wasserstein contraction.
The finite diagnostic is not formal verification of the general theorem; the theorem is proved directly in the report.

experiment.result: Exact enumeration over all spin boundary assignments gives max row sum 0.5, center column sum 1.5, unweighted coupled drift +0.5, and weighted margin 0.5 for weights (1, 1/3, 1/3, 1/3).
experiment.verification: python3 star_check.py exits successfully with assertions for the influence formula, row/column sums, drift, and weighted condition.
experiment.interpretation: Mechanism diagnostic only; not a necessity result and not a comparison against all possible couplings.
